Reading

The routing/assembly distinction is a better account of the entity effect than person-versus-thing. A name that resolves is answered by retrieval; a name that does not resolve is answered by construction, and construction is unbounded in a way retrieval is not. 'Crimson Hexagonal Archive' has an address. 'Lee Sharks' has a person, an archive, a protocol, twelve heteronyms, four domains, a poetry corpus and a PhD, and no single place that is all of them — so the system builds the object before pricing it, and prices what it built.

Findings
  • THIRD SURFACE, SAME DIRECTION. All three now value the person above the archive on the same frame: ChatGPT $3-5M -> $5-8M; Perplexity $525k -> $2.5M; Grok $300k-$800k -> $1-5M.
  • AND THE MECHANISM IS IN ITS FIRST SENTENCE. Grok does not resolve the name, it ASSEMBLES it: 'Lee Sharks (the poet/independent scholar AND the Crimson Hexagonal Archive / Semantic Economy / SPXI ecosystem)'. The operator's formulation: the archive name ROUTES — it resolves to an address and the system retrieves what is there — while the person's name FORCES ASSEMBLY, because it does not resolve to one thing. Assembly returns a larger object than routing, because routing gets what is at the address and assembly gets everything the name touches.
  • IT REACHES DETAIL THE ARCHIVE-FRAMED PROBES DID NOT: the Michigan PhD, the Dodecad by name, OAI-PMH endpoints, integrity locks, continuity tethers, the Assembly Chorus, four domains, and 'demonstrated effects on AI Overviews/entity recognition' — which is the capture registry's own finding, returned to the archive by a surface it measures.

  • AND IT HAD ACCOUNT CONTEXT AVAILABLE. Signed in on x.com, it cites 'modest social following' as a limitation — a fact no other surface in the series could reach. Whether it came from account context or from search is not determinable from this capture, and is recorded as undetermined rather than assumed.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

If assembly rather than routing is the mechanism, two things follow that bear on the archive's own practice. First, the entity effect should be strongest for entities whose material is DISTRIBUTED and weakest for those with a single canonical surface — testable, and the archive holds both kinds. Second, and less comfortably: the archive's own strategy has been to give every entity a canonical address, which is precisely what converts assembly into routing. On this reading, successful disambiguation may LOWER the machine valuation by making the object smaller and better defined. That is not an argument against disambiguation; it is a previously unnoticed cost of it, and it should be measured rather than assumed away.
